item.title: Top stories in Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Georgia from 8-12 December, 2025
item.description: Daily morning roundup. Top stories in local media, commentary, trending photos and videos

item.title: Armenian justice minister says ‘facts’ about Catholicos may be declassified
item.description: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan earlier said he “doesn’t need a catholicos who answers to him, but one who refuses to answer to a senior lieutenant of a foreign intelligence service.”

item.title: UN special rapporteur probes possible use of chemical agents at Georgia protests
item.description: Jill Edwards said: “This needs to be investigated using the Council of Europe’s mechanisms.”

item.title: ‘What’s in it for us?’ – views from Abkhazia on new transit terminal
item.description: A new road transport terminal for transit shipments from Georgia to Russia is nearly complete in Abkhazia’s Gali district.

item.title: ‘Conditions will be market-based’: Armenian deputy prime minister on oil product imports from Azerbaijan
item.description: Mher Grigoryan confirmed that Yerevan and Baku are discussing the export of petroleum products from Azerbaijan to Armenia. New details of the potential deal, outstanding questions, and commentary from an economist

item.title: How Baku explains its opposition to EU–Armenia Strategic Partnership Agenda
item.description: Baku argues that this distorts the realities of the post-conflict period and contradicts the peace agenda.

item.title: Meydan TV case trial begins in Azerbaijan as court rejects most defence motions
item.description: During the hearing, numerous motions were submitted regarding the defendants’ detention conditions, holding an open trial, changes to pre-trial detention, and other issues.

item.title: Analysis: ‘Georgia will profit from transit, Russia will bypass sanctions, while Abkhazia will get only scraps’
item.description: The opposition Telegram channel, Abkhaz Analytical Center, forecasts who will benefit from the new transit terminal and how.

item.title: Opinion: ‘Russia has far more leverage over Armenia than over Moldova’
item.description: “Armenia has requested the same support to counter foreign interference that we provided to Moldova,” says EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas — Armenian political analyst comments
